t: 'Freedom from the Chain'… K-Escalator Flagship Woochang Innotech Officially Launches K-Roborator, the World's First 'Distributed-Power Circulation Escalator' That Sheds a Century-Old Drive Method

blocks.cap: K-Roborator, the world's first distributed-power circulation escalator unveiled by Woochang Innotech. Its slogan, "Beyond 100 Years of Chains," declares that it goes beyond the century-old chain. | Provided by Woochang Innotech

blocks.x: Woochang Innotech, which brands itself as the flagship company of "K-Escalator," has officially launched K-Roborator, the world's first distributed-power circulation escalator. By stripping away the centralized chain-drive method that has continued for nearly 100 years since the early 1900s and planting a compact motor in each and every step so it rolls on its own, the company has completed a robot-type escalator with homegrown technology — and that is drawing the industry's attention.
Shedding the 100-year-old chain entirely… "The world's first self-propelled escalator that rolls on its own, with a motor in every step"

The heart of K-Roborator is "distributed power." Where a conventional escalator hauled dozens of steps at once with a single large motor, a chain and a reduction gear, K-Roborator places a compact motor and reduction gear in each step a passenger rides on, so the steps move on their own. It is the same principle as an electric vehicle with a motor on every wheel.

As a result, the chain and sprocket, the large drive unit and the machine room have all disappeared. Mechanical problems that had recurred for decades — chain-tension changes, sprocket wear, lubrication management — were eliminated as well. Woochang Innotech said this structure cut the number of parts by roughly half, lowered raw-material costs by 40 to 50 percent versus Chinese products, and reduced electricity costs by 30 to 40 percent.

The motor efficiency is also far ahead. While an AC motor used in escalators stays at 65 to 68 percent, the BLDC motor developed in-house by Woochang Innotech reaches 90 percent or more, and up to 98 percent in precision control mounted with a dedicated semiconductor. The company explains that it designed even the central-processing semiconductor that computes and controls the motor, making it the only such technology held anywhere in the world.

blocks.cap: A 3D concept rendering showing that K-Roborator, which freely traverses flat ground, stairs and slopes, can even be installed in special terrain such as a cave tourist site. | Provided by Woochang Innotech

blocks.x: Traversing flat ground, hills and stairs as one body… "Change only the rail length and there is no terrain it cannot climb"

The point where K-Roborator decisively parts ways with conventional escalators is "terrain." Unlike the old method that only went up and down a straight incline, this product moves horizontally across flat sections like a moving walkway, climbs stairs, crosses a gentle hill and then continues onto flat ground again — handling a composite route as a single body.

The secret lies in the absence of the chain and the large rail that once bound the steps. Because each step moves on an independent motor and they connect by biting and releasing one another, changing only the shape and length of the rail reproduces any route in which horizontal, stair and slope sections are mixed. It is a design made possible because everything needed for drive is contained inside the step.

There is no floor-count limit either. Simply by adding step modules, five floors or ten floors are tied into a single circulation route. A conventional escalator had to enlarge its motor capacity the longer it grew, but K-Roborator, with power scattered across every step, connects endlessly not only across multiple department-store floors but also up the long slopes of mountainous terrain without strain.

blocks.cap: Woochang Innotech's other core patent, K-Roborator's circulation drive structure. In this method a step rises, crosses over to the side and comes back down, replacing the conventional structure that required one unit each (two motor sets) for up and down. Like a pulley, the ascending and descending sides mesh into a single loop so that, just as an elevator rises and falls by counterweight, the force of the descending steps pulls the ascending steps up. Thanks to this pulley principle, the electricity-saving effect is large. Provided by Woochang Innotech
A conventional escalator takes six months to a year to replace, but K-Roborator lets you swap only the step module in a few hours. | Provided by Woochang Innotech

blocks.x: One unit does the work of two… "The economics of the circulation type, where a step that rises crosses over and comes back down"

K-Roborator's other axis is the "circulation type" embedded in its very name. A conventional escalator had to install one unit each for ascent and descent, but this product operates as a single circulation loop in which a step rises, crosses over to the side and comes back down again. One unit does the work of two.

The maintenance method has also changed. Because the step and motor are bound together in a module, when a fault occurs you need not tear down the entire installation — you simply swap out that module. It is a solution that squarely targets the reality in which domestic escalators, relying 100 percent on imports, had to halt operations for nearly a year for a single replacement.

Energy efficiency stands out too. A regenerative system that turns the gravitational energy generated during descent back into electricity cuts 30 to 50 percent of annual total power and 20 to 40 percent of peak power. By reducing 6.2 to 10.4 tons of carbon dioxide per unit a year, it is described as a next-generation transport facility that meets eco-friendly building certification and ESG management goals.
K-Roborator's modular maintenance method, lifting out only the module in which the step and motor are bound together.

blocks.cap: K-Roborator's modular maintenance method, lifting out only the module in which the step and motor are bound together. | Provided by Woochang Innotech
K-Roborator's distributed-power structure, with a compact BLDC motor and bearing integrated inside each step, shown alongside the actual step module and motor. | Provided by Woochang Innotech

blocks.x: Even when it stops, no one falls… "With no chain, there is nothing to snap and no domino-style tumble"

A large share of escalator accidents originate when a chain snaps, the steps run backward and riders are swept down and fall all at once. K-Roborator has no chain at all, blocking this danger at the source. What links the steps is a connecting device that bites and releases together with the rail, so there is no drive element that can break.

With a distributed-power structure in which an independent motor is attached to every step, its fault tolerance is also high. Even if one motor stops, the rest take over the drive so the whole does not halt, and which motor on which step has developed a fault is shown in real time on the control panel. It is a design that prevents a single fault from spreading into a system-wide chain paralysis.

It is safe even during a power outage. A motor equipped with a servo function, even when the power is cut, does not stop abruptly but comes gently to a halt along a programmed deceleration curve. Operating noise is 5 to 10 decibels lower on average and vibration about 30 percent lower, so it proves its worth at facilities sensitive to noise, such as airports, hospitals and mixed-use malls.

blocks.cap: Woochang Innotech Chairman Lee Jang-mun explains K-Roborator's distributed-power structure, with a motor planted in every step. | Photo - AVING News reporter Choi Min

blocks.x: What Woochang Innotech Chairman Lee Jang-mun emphasizes most is the "building exterior." Chairman Lee said, "Because it freely traverses flat ground, hills and stairs, and its route can be laid out in any shape like a circular track, K-Roborator can be installed as if climbing up and down a building's outer wall," adding, "The transport facility itself becomes the building's exterior design."

Chairman Lee stressed, "If you create a route that winds up the outer wall of a large sculpture at a tourist site or a landmark facility, the means of transport itself becomes a spectacle," and, "Because there is no machine room or large drive unit, it attaches nimbly even to constrained locations such as a facility wall, so it will establish itself as a tourism resource and a design object that replaces monorails and inclined elevators."
Everything that moves is a robot… "The escalator that becomes a robot — K-Roborator rewrites mobility"​​​​​​​

The product name "K-Roborator" carries a direction that fuses robot and escalator. Woochang Innotech sees not only humanoids but every self-moving object as a robot, and envisions evolving the escalator, too, beyond a mere transport facility into a robot that embraces AI and sensors.

The potential for expansion comes from here as well. It can display targeted advertising that recognizes the boarding situation, and can also be applied as a stair-type conveyor that carries cargo or freight. Like electric-wheelchair support that goes up and down stairs, it also extends into mobility-convenience technology for the elderly and the transport-vulnerable.

At the root of this vision is Chairman Lee Jang-mun's 47 years in the elevator business. As a first-generation figure in Korea's elevator industry, he led the division at Hanyang Group's Hanyang Gongyoung, and personally acquired that division during the foreign-exchange crisis. Over the following 20-odd years he devoted himself to research and development, unveiling one after another an emergency-call device that connects straight to a control center when someone is trapped in an elevator, and, during the COVID period, the world's first rotating sterilization button for elevators. Now his determination to change an elevator technology that had stood still for 100 years has carried through to K-Roborator.

Woochang Innotech aims to establish itself, with K-Roborator at the fore, as a bona fide "K-Escalator" flagship company. Its goal is to localize the development, production and maintenance of a domestic market that has leaned 100 percent on imports, and to turn back to Korea a history of escalators in which the United States was the birthplace. It has filed two patents each in Korea and the United States, and — championing people's right to safe mobility — is also challenging for a CES 2027 Innovation Award.

t: [Pangyo Interview] PCNC, Founded by a Computer Engineering Ph.D. and Former Elementary School Teacher, Innovates Reading Habits with Socratic AI Conversations and 10,000 Books

blocks.cap: CEO Duckki Kim of PCNC | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: EdTech enterprise PCNC (CEO Duckki Kim) is drawing significant attention across domestic and international education markets through a customized reading solution integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and big data technologies. TOAPING—an acronym for ‘Technical Oriented, Attractive, Personal, Interest Network Gateway’—developed by PCNC provides personalized Korean reading and learning services tailored to learners’ specific proficiency levels and personal interests.

Duckki Kim, CEO of PCNC, holds a Ph.D. in Computer Engineering and built his career as an elementary school teacher, university professor, and executive at major IT enterprises. During his time as an elementary school teacher, he witnessed systemic issues in education where students became immersed in short-term rote learning without voluntary interest or lost interest in reading altogether due to mandatory reading programs. As a result, many students suffered significant learning gaps after entering middle and high school from a lack of foundational reading habits. To resolve these issues, leveraging experiences from two successful corporate exits, he established PCNC as an EdTech enterprise to innovatively support public education environments.

The core differentiator of the TOAPING service lies in proprietary technologies and methodologies that foster self-directed learning. Based on SQ3R—a proven reading education methodology—the platform provides Korean books, traditional fairy tales, and cultural classics. At the same time, its hybrid machine learning-based AI recommendation engine analyzes individual user interests to recommend up to 20 real-time curated book selections aligned with each learner’s focus. In particular, unlike conventional AI tools that merely provide fast answers to user questions, TOAPING’s AI service implements a ‘Socratic AI service’ that poses guiding counter-questions to learners—akin to the question-and-answer method of philosopher Socrates—forcing them to think independently and arrive at solutions themselves. Furthermore, to motivate learning, it features a goal achievement support system combining milestone setting with digital rewards, functioning as a virtual library by securing approximately 10,000 Korean e-book content titles.

blocks.cap: Main page of the website introducing TOAPING. | Image courtesy of PCNC

blocks.x: As of late 2024, PCNC has achieved strong growth by securing over 23,000 student members across 250 schools in South Korea. Its business model operates on a subscription-based structure, providing annual institutional subscriptions to schools and libraries, while offering monthly subscriptions to private educational institutions and individual learners. Steps toward global market expansion are accelerating as well. The company signed a TOAPING reading service contract with the elementary division of Tokyo Korean School in Japan, executed master distribution contracts for Japan and Germany to conduct local Proof of Concept (PoC) testing, and established a local entity in Germany. Having identified a shortage of quality Korean educational reading content at York University in Canada in 2019, CEO Kim reinforced content to build a stepping stone for global entry, actively promoting partnerships with overseas universities offering Korean language departments, Korean heritage language schools, churches, and private educational institutions targeting future entry into the US market.

PCNC plans to unveil ‘TOAPING Version 3’ this year, a next-generation solution where conversational AI leads learning situations by integrating generative LLM, RAG, and multi-vector embedding AI agents. Additionally, the company accelerates technological refinement to leap into a global HabitTech enterprise by expanding its reading service domain into all academic curriculum subjects and introducing multilingual services. PCNC plans to broaden its global recognition further by scheduling participation in CES 2027.

AVING News met with PCNC CEO Duckki Kim at the Startup Campus in Pangyo Techno Valley to discuss their Socratic AI engine, digital library ecosystem, and global HabitTech expansion strategy. Reporter Thomas Frederiksen conducted the interview.

Q1. Thomas Frederiksen, Reporter: Hello everyone, and thank you for joining us here today at the Pangyo Techno Valley Startup Campus. My next guest is the CEO of PCNC, Mr. Duckki Kim. Welcome! Could you tell me a little bit about your company, PCNC?

A. Duckki Kim, CEO of PCNC: At PCNC, as an edtech company, we want everyone to be able to study according to their individual level and personal interests. To make that possible, we developed our core technologies using AI, big data, and blockchain.
Q2. What problem did you observe in the field that inspired you to start this company, and what was the primary problem you set out to solve?

A. Duckki Kim: When I was teaching, I noticed that students and parents always want to study hard, but students often prioritize short-term fun over building core habits. By the time students transition to middle or high school, parents and students are often surprised to find they lack proper reading habits and foundational literacy skills. My primary goal was to create a solution to solve that specific problem.
Q3. What exactly is TOAPING, and how does it help students build focused reading habits?

A. Duckki Kim: “TOAPING” stands for Technical Oriented, Attractive, Personal, Interest Network Gateway. We focus heavily on two key factors: a student’s personal interest and their reading level. We want every student to enjoy reading, so we promote “focused reading”—known in Korea as Pond Reading (immersing oneself deeply in a topic). By doing this, a student’s area of interest and concern expands naturally as they read.
Q4. How do you integrate artificial intelligence into this recommendation service?

A. Duckki Kim: Since 2022, we have been researching and developing a machine learning-based AI recommendation engine. We created a hybrid recommendation approach that analyzes student interest to recommend real-time curated book selections—offering up to 20 tailored books per individual user.
Q5. Standard AI tools typically give direct answers, but your platform uses AI to enhance a student’s critical thinking. Could you explain how your Socratic AI service works?

A. Duckki Kim: Normally, AI services are used to find quick answers or results. However, in the learning process, simply answering doesn’t help the student grow. We designed an AI agent that asks guiding questions. When a student answers, the AI agent evaluates their response and asks the next logical question, forcing the student to think deeply for themselves rather than relying on easy answers. It operates on the Socratic method to guide learning through targeted questioning.

blocks.cap: Mobile user interface of TOAPING. Featuring a vast library, reading or saving lists is effortless, and its book recommendation algorithm suggests suitable books. | Image courtesy of PCNC

blocks.x: Q6. Is this platform exclusively for native Korean speakers, or can it also be used by international students learning Korean?

A. Duckki Kim: Ultimately, our vision is to expand globally. While we started in Korea, literacy is a universal need for children worldwide. Currently, we serve two primary markets: K–9 reading habit development for school students, and a Korean digital library service for global users learning Korean as a foreign language.
Q7. Do you already have experience expanding into international markets outside of Korea?

A. Duckki Kim: Yes! Back in 2019, York University in Canada used our early service for students studying Korean. At the time, we were still early in development and realized global learners faced a major shortage of quality Korean reading content. That led us to fully integrate our TOAPING reading platform with an extensive digital content library. Last year, Tokyo Korean School in Japan adopted our service as well.
Q8. What are your future expansion plans for the platform in terms of academic subjects, language support, and entry into the US market?

A. Duckki Kim: We are expanding our reading and Korean language services globally while actively conducting R&D to broaden our scope beyond reading into all academic school subjects. Furthermore, we are developing multi-language support beyond Korean. Later this year or early next year, we plan to introduce TOAPING Version 3.0, which features an upgraded questioning AI agent that can interactively guide complete learning scenarios across various subjects. For the US market, we plan to introduce our service to US universities—specifically targeting Korean language departments—as well as Korean language heritage schools, church-affiliated education programs, and community study groups. Subscribing to TOAPING grants unlimited access to our entire virtual library of over 10,000 Korean e-books anytime, anywhere.
Q9. Finally, operating out of Pangyo Techno Valley, what makes this location attractive for an edtech startup like PCNC?

A. Duckki Kim: People often refer to Pangyo as Korea’s Silicon Valley. The area brings together a high concentration of leading IT, software, and AI companies. Being located here among industry peers provides fantastic cooperation and has proven to be a great strategic decision for our growth.

t: [Interview] In Search of 'The Single Pill That Fits My Body'… The Journey to Launching the Health Platform 'APHDA' - CEO Heo Yong-ho of Apharm Health

blocks.cap: Heo Yong, CEO of Apharm Health, explains the company's growth story and the future direction of the health platform 'APHDA.' He spoke about the path of 'authenticity one step ahead' that he has walked, starting from sales in pharmacies and hospitals and extending to AI. | Photo - AVING News Reporter Choi Min

blocks.x: Anyone who has ever bought nutritional supplements has likely harbored this doubt at least once: "Do I really need all these pills?" Starting from that very question, Heo Yong, CEO of Apharm Health, is developing a service where AI reads your health data and helps you select only what you need.

What is interesting is the path he has walked to reach this point. The boy who dreamed of becoming a vocalist has worked at pharmacy counters and in hospital sales, riding the massive waves of online shopping malls, COVID-19, and AI a step ahead of others at every turn.

The secret, surprisingly, was not a grandiose strategy. Instead of competing similarly to others, it was entirely about the sincerity of creating something that didn't exist before and filling it with truly good products. It is a path where the genuine sincerity of sales, learned face-to-face, has led to products and, in turn, to the power to connect with consumers.

A journey that began with taking on all the responsibilities at his father's pharmacy… "In his senior year of high school, he was already in the field during the turbulent era of the separation of prescribing and dispensing of medicines."

Heo Yong, CEO of Apharm Health, had his first job at a pharmacy invested in by his father, who now manages Apharm. Here, he gained firsthand experience in all aspects of pharmacy operations—including inventory management, ordering, store support, and customer service—learning both people and the field simultaneously.

His beginning was not just early, but fast. In his senior year of high school, during a turbulent period when the separation of prescribing and dispensing was just taking root, he was already standing on the front lines. Although he was originally a young man in the arts and humanities preparing for vocal music, the pharmacy counter became his first stage instead of singing.

What led him down the path of the pharmaceutical industry were the pharmaceutical company executives who frequented the pharmacy. Saying, "They looked so sophisticated, wearing nice suits and conversing with people with sparkling eyes," he resolved to join a pharmaceutical company after completing his military service. Indeed, after his discharge, he jumped straight into the sales field, and his path naturally led from pharmacy sales to hospital sales.

Looking back, that early start was the foundation of everything. At an age when others were contemplating their career paths in college, he learned the dynamics of distribution and hospitals firsthand; the roots of his future sense for planning products and designing platforms grew right here.

blocks.cap: Heo Yong, CEO of Apharm Health Co., Ltd., is giving a tour at the company's headquarters office in Daegu. | Photo - AVING News Reporter Choi Min

blocks.x: A Young Man Who Used to Visit Hospitals with Watermelons in the Summer… “In the End, It’s All About People”

Sales of pharmaceutical supplies to hospitals are often referred to as the "flower of sales." It is the most challenging stage, offering the greatest learning opportunities; however, a young man fresh out of military service honed his business acumen in this rugged environment and rose to the position of General Manager within just six months of joining the company.

His approach was always about people. While pharmaceutical sales representatives are typically relegated to the background in hospitals where patient care always takes precedence, he found the answer in his relationships with the hospital staff. During the sweltering summer, he would buy watermelons, prepare them, and take them to the hospitals to look after the employees with great care.

"While others visited six or seven places a day, I visited eight or ten." The connections he forged through such tireless legwork were not short-lived. Even as time passed, these relationships endured, and it is said that there are still quite a few managers at the hospitals in Daegu who remember him.

Ultimately, what he learned was that people are everything. This principle of winning hearts before products solidified in the field during those years and became an unwavering standard throughout his career of creating products and building brands. Expanding His Perspective on Cosmetics Distributed to Hospitals and Clinics … "Beyond Medicine, I Learned About Products and the Distribution Field with My Whole Body"

His next stage was his father's company. A proposal to go beyond simply selling medicine and instead create cosmetics distributed to hospitals and clinics led him into the world of products, and thus he became a member of the first generation in Korea to encounter the concept of cosmeceuticals, which combine cosmetics and medicine.

He planned and supplied cosmetics and moisturizing products for hospitals and clinics, accumulating extensive experience in both product development and the medical distribution field. This experience of handling materials and concepts ahead of others served as the foundation for later creating his own brand.

blocks.cap: The product line of 'Petit N,' a premium health supplement brand that even pregnant women can consume with peace of mind. On display is a lineup that has consistently raised the quality of products safe for the whole family to consume, including the 100% vegan plant-based 'National Omega-3,' the 'National CalMaDi' (Calcium, Magnesium, Vitamin D), the 'National T.A.G. Enzyme,' Iron C+, and pregnancy and childbirth gift sets. | Photo - AVING News Reporter Choi Min

Petit N 'Vericitol Gummy'. This is a new product recently introduced by Apharm Health that is garnering attention. Inositol, the key ingredient, is a highly sought-after component among those interested in hormone balance and women's health management. It is sought after by a wide range of users, from adolescent women around the time of their first menstruation to adult women looking to monitor their menstrual cycles and overall condition, as well as those preparing for pregnancy. Just three gummies a day provide 2,000mg of myo-inositol, and the product features a sweet and sour taste enhanced by the addition of cranberry and blueberry concentrates. Applied as a chewable gummy that eliminates the hassle of powder formulations, the company introduces it as Korea's first jelly-type inositol product. | Photo - Aving News Reporter Park Yu-jin

blocks.x: "The person I love needs to take it… The iron supplement I made myself for my wife became the premium brand 'Petit N'"

And finally, he stood on his own. CEO Heo Yong established Apharm Health as a sole proprietorship in 2012, and after growing the business, converted it into a corporation in 2021. It operates independently as a separate entity from his father's Apharm.

The decisive turning point came around the time of his marriage. Unable to find a suitable iron supplement for his wife, he decided to make it himself. Drawing on his experience in the pharmaceutical distribution field, he dedicated a couple of months to the project and completed his first in-house product, which led to the premium brand Petit N, which even pregnant women can consume with peace of mind.

"The person I love needs to take it, so I can't just give them anything." His product philosophy is encapsulated in this single statement. Thus, his principle of prioritizing quality over margins soon earned recognition from the market, and hospitals that had been using other products began switching to his own one by one.
"We also created the name Kalmadhi…" "From Probiotics to Plant-Based Omega-3, Always at the Forefront"

Probiotics served as a springboard for his leap forward. Taking note that 60 to 70 percent of Koreans cannot properly digest lactose in milk, he launched Lacto-U under the concept of "easy-to-digest, stomach-friendly probiotics," and expanded it into a "Sensitive" line targeting sensitive intestines.

This quality translated into tangible results. He differentiated his products as high-bacterial probiotics by raising the guaranteed number of live bacteria reaching the intestines to 10 billion. He offered a direct, different answer to a market that had previously emphasized only low bacterial counts.

His sense for naming was also exceptional. He was the first to coin the term "CalMaDi" for a product combining calcium, magnesium, and vitamin D; while many companies now use the same name, it was undoubtedly Apharm Health that pioneered that category.

The same was true for Omega-3. At a time when refined animal oils were the mainstream, he introduced plant-based Omega-3, making it easy to consume without any fishy smell or aversion. With the capsules also made 100 percent vegan, this product earned the trust of pregnant women and mothers raising children.

blocks.cap: In an interview, CEO Heo Yong explains the journey of his journey, which began in the pharmaceutical distribution field and led to cosmeceuticals, a proprietary online store, and the AI platform 'Apda'. His philosophy is that "winning hearts face-to-face is no different from creating good products." | Photo - Aving News Reporter Choi Min

blocks.x: Shifting direction to online, COVID-19 expanded the market… "Just as Baedal Minjok did, the times give wings to those who are prepared."

His good material gained popularity through word of mouth, but he did not stop there. He shifted his distribution direction to online in a market where offline sales were everything, building his own online shopping mall that sells both cosmetics and health supplements ahead of the industry.

COVID-19 proved that his judgment was correct. At a time when contactless consumption exploded and even visiting hospitals became difficult, products known through word of mouth exploded online all at once. Much like Baedal Minjok's rapid growth during that period, the times effectively gave wings to those who were prepared.

He reflects that preparing for the flow of the times one year ahead of others was decisive. In fact, his own online store handling both health supplements and cosmeceuticals was virtually the only one at the time. That sense of being a step ahead propelled Apharm Health forward during every moment of crisis.
Divided by 'My Health Information' rather than advertisements or trends… "So, I established a research institute and accumulated data."

Then, another turning point arrived. He diagnosed that, following the cosmetics market, the health functional food market also entered a "red ocean" about two years ago. With the rapid increase in companies and advertising agencies, the situation reached a point where products alone were no longer the answer.

His response was organization. He established a corporate research institute and embarked on the development of the health platform, Apda. His starting point was, "We established a corporate research institute and accumulated data to help consumers choose products based on their own health information, rather than advertisements or trends."

He summarizes the relationship between the two businesses as follows: If Petit N is a health functional food brand that has improved the quality of products suitable for families, Apda is a platform that improves the quality of products consumers can choose for themselves.

The direction of his deliberations was clear. He envisioned a personalized service that helps consumers select the perfect product tailored to their individual health information, rather than the method of buying products simply because they are advertised as good.

blocks.cap: The main screen of 'APHDA,' a public data-based AI health supplement recommendation platform. By allowing users to converse with a chatbot to independently explore health concerns, product recommendations, and symptom analysis, it helps users select products based on their personal health information rather than advertisements. | Provided by Apharm Health Co., Ltd.

blocks.x: Reading my health data, not crawling... "Combining 50,000 registered health supplements in Korea with my checkup results to select only what is necessary."

Born from this idea, APHDA is a hyper-personalized AI health supplement recommendation agent based on public data. It analyzes approximately 50,000 registered health supplements in Korea in combination with the user's health checkup data to pinpoint the exact amount needed. It resolves health concerns as if conversing with a chatbot.

The starting point was a long-standing contradiction in the market. Middle-aged and older adults spend between 200,000 and 500,000 won on nutritional supplements every month, yet there was no way to verify their effectiveness. Because they relied on YouTube and blog marketing for their choices, a structure had solidified where claims of health benefits were rampant, but actual satisfaction remained low.

Therefore, APHDA analyzes checkup results and individual inquiries together to recommend only the appropriate amount needed. The vision is to reduce the monthly expenditure on supplements from the 400,000 won range to the 100,000 won range; the explanation is that this cost savings comes not from cutting prices, but from accurately selecting only what is necessary. Above all, the basis of trust is data. According to the company, Apda has accumulated over 300 million pieces of proprietary data by refining and integrating national public data from sources such as the National Health Insurance Service and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, rather than through web crawling. The company explains that it manages data using an on-premise method without utilizing external cloud services.
Neither Diagnosis Nor Prescription, but a Service to Help with Choices… "Recommendations Prioritize My Health Suitability Over Our Own Products"

To avoid misunderstandings, the company clarifies a key point. Apda is not a medical service that diagnoses diseases or provides treatment and prescriptions; rather, it is a non-medical service that assists individuals in selecting health functional foods suited to their needs.

As the company also sells its own brand, Petit &, neutrality in recommendations is a critical task. Regarding this, the company stated that recommendations prioritize health suitability, the possibility of duplicate consumption, and cautionary ingredients over whether the product is its own. Furthermore, the company plans to transparently display whether a product is its own brand or an advertisement or partnership item so that users can distinguish between them.

Given that it handles sensitive health information, it has also established protection principles. It is the company's policy that health information provided by users with their consent is processed in accordance with relevant laws and internal security standards, and that core analysis data and models are managed within the company's infrastructure.

blocks.cap: Commendations, certifications, and brand awards received by Apharm are displayed side by side. This is a space where the company’s track record of leading the way in product development and distribution has been built upon the foundation of trust. Using this accumulated trust as a springboard, Apharm Health is now taking its next step with "Aphda," an AI platform designed to help consumers select products that suit them. From product quality to the quality of choice, that display case points to both the path traveled and the path ahead. | Photo - Aving News Reporter Choi Min

blocks.x: The July launch is just the beginning… "We will create a full-stack ecosystem that connects health like Baedal Minjok, extending to doorstep delivery by 2029."

The roadmap is structured in three stages. First, a service recommending health supplements will be launched officially in July 2026. The core of Stage 1 is the experience of users actively finding products suited to them by conversing with a chatbot. This is the result of approximately three years of private refinement.

Next, in Stage 2 in 2027, personalized ingredient recipes will be derived through reinforcement learning verification. It will move beyond simply selecting off-the-shelf products to a customized stage that proposes the optimal combination of health supplement ingredients tailored to an individual's health condition.

Finally, the goal for the final stage in 2029 is a full-stack ecosystem. It integrates personal health data, customized product formulations, and doorstep delivery into a single system. The structure ensures that conversations with a mobile chatbot translate into optimal ingredient combinations, directly leading to last-mile delivery. It aims to become a so-called "health version of Baedal Minjok."

A vision for expansion is also being drawn. Moving forward, Apda aims to become a central hub connecting integrated services such as fitness, logistics, insurtech, and fintech. Its first global gateway is the CES 2027 Innovation Award, and the company is determined to launch into the global market with a service that combines health checkup data with AI to deliver customized solutions.
Crisis or Opportunity? The waves have always been on the side of the prepared… "From Product Quality to the Quality of Choice"

Looking back, his growth has always been driven by two axes. One was the decisive move to seize major opportunities such as online shopping malls, COVID-19, and AI; the other was the small, steady attempts made in between, half a step ahead of others.

In fact, these attempts included coining the name "Calmadi" and being the first to launch products that did not exist in the world, such as plant-based Omega-3 and Korea's first jelly-type inositol. Because he was already rowing before the big waves arrived, he was able to ride the opportunity when it came.

And the word that runs through all these attempts is authenticity. He believes that winning people's hearts face-to-face, creating high-quality products, and helping consumers choose the products that suit them are no different. In a sense, the hands that have focused on improving product quality are now moving toward enhancing the quality of choice.

Regarding the AI ​​era, some call it a crisis, while others see it as an opportunity. However, the young man who once dreamed of becoming a vocalist has already set his answer and is rowing his boat. The principle of creating something that did not exist before—first, yet with sincerity—is the path that CEO Heo Yong of Apharm Health has walked and will walk in the future.

t: [CES Innovation Awards 2027 Special] MAKEMAKE Heads to CES 2027 with ‘PERLUO’, a Non-Powered Tumbler Creating Soft Water in 60 Seconds by Shaking… “Solving Problems Caused by Water Through Materials”

blocks.cap: Hyoseob Kwak, CEO of MAKEMAKE, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: MAKEMAKE (CEO Hyoseob Kwak) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held on July 30. Organizers arranged this meetup to inform overseas media about participating companies’ products and technologies in advance for global markets while expanding business opportunities. MAKEMAKE is a chemical-based beauty-tech startup solving problems water leaves on skin and hair through material technology. It will unveil its new non-powered portable soft water tumbler ‘PERLUO’ for the first time at CES in January 2027. CEO Hyoseob Kwak delivered the presentation on this day.

It started with swimming. Swimming pool water contains chloramines (residual chlorine) formed by combining chlorine with body secretions, which regular shampoos fail to remove effectively, and products caring for scalp and hair after swimming were non-existent. MAKEMAKE resolved this issue with its self-developed zeolite composite material technology, ‘ZeoDualite™’. According to the company, this material removes up to 98% of residual chlorine based on external evaluations. In October 2024, the company first introduced ‘SOOO’, a swim-exclusive shampoo brand applying this material. In July 2025, the company completed patent registration for ZeoDualite™.

blocks.cap: App screen of MAKEMAKE’s non-powered portable soft water tumbler ‘PERLUO’ | Provided by MAKEMAKE

blocks.x: Established in May 2024, MAKEMAKE formed its team with CEO Hyoseob Kwak—boasting e-commerce and beauty new business experience—alongside a technical lead holding a Ph.D. in chemistry and experience at EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, Switzerland), and a creative lead who won all three of the world’s top design awards (Red Dot, iF, IDEA). Featuring a full-stack structure that places front-end capabilities in planning, branding, marketing, global expansion, and operations alongside back-end capabilities in R&D, research infrastructure, and manufacturing know-how within a single company, the company promotes its strength in maintaining short development cycles without outsourcing, reflecting market signals directly into material development.

PERLUO, unveiled for the first time at CES, represents the first product expanding from swimming pool care to ‘water stress care’. When users pour tap water, insert a replaceable cartridge, and shake for about 60 seconds, water repeatedly passes through the cartridge material, filtering out hardness components (calcium, magnesium) and trace metals originating from aging pipes. The porous framework captures calcium and magnesium, while chelating functional groups bind metals. Requiring no pumps, piping, or external power, users can operate it identically at home, hotels, or gyms, while repeatedly using the main body and replacing cartridges to drive recurring subscription re-orders. MAKEMAKE aims to address water environment-specific issues—such as residual chlorine, hard water minerals, heavy metals from aging pipes, and seawater salinity—with respective dedicated materials.

blocks.cap: MAKEMAKE CEO Hyoseob Kwak (left) during an interview with Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Achievements accumulate continuously as well. SOOO entered major channels including domestic Health & Beauty (H&B) stores, department store pop-ups, major messenger gifting platforms, and in-flight duty-free shops, with company mall membership exceeding 20,000 members. Collaborations on luxury hotel amenities and official sponsorships of national swimming competitions progress in parallel. Overseas, the company opened an official brand store on Amazon North America, maintaining a 4.8 rating for its children’s swim-care products, while completing US trademark registration and FDA approvals. With a Brazilian distributor, the company achieved an initial export of 100,000 USD with chelating products designed to remove heavy metals from aging pipes, while earning adoption in Turkish premium salons and UAE luxury hotels. In November 2025, the company won the Grand Prize in the Haircare category at Asia’s largest beauty exhibition, and in January 2026, earned the Grand Prize at the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ ‘K-Beauty in Shanghai’.

Financial performance grew from 5 billion KRW in revenue in 2025 (500 million KRW in exports) to 5.8 billion KRW in the first half of 2026, targeting 12 billion KRW annually. In terms of investment, seed funding attraction was followed by selections for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups TIPS and IBK Changgong 15th batch. MAKEMAKE plans sequential expansion into Europe, South America, and Japan led by Amazon North America, internalizing material development and validation centered around its corporate research institute established in January 2026. Commercialization of hair loss alleviation technology based on Viola mandshurica extract transferred from a research institution under the Ministry of Environment is in preparation as well.

blocks.cap: Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen (left) and MAKEMAKE CEO Hyoseob Kwak take a commemorative photo after concluding the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Hyoseob Kwak, CEO of MAKEMAKE, stated, “Water stress is not severe in Korea because tap water is soft, but hair and skin damage from minerals and heavy metals runs far more serious in the US, Europe, and South America.” He added, “Residual chlorine, minerals, heavy metals, and salinity ultimately stem from a single problem rooted in water, and we will solve this comprehensively through material technology.” He continued, saying, “We will demonstrate that K-beauty possesses competitiveness not only in formulations and marketing but also in core material technologies, growing from swimming pools into a brand managing all water-induced issues.”

t: [CES Innovation Awards 2027 Special] AES Tech Challenges CES 2027 Innovation Awards with ‘ammoNOVA Ultra’, an On-Site Hydrogen Extraction System from Ammonia Targeting AI Data Center Power Demands

blocks.cap: Jaehong Jeffrey Chun, CEO of AES Tech, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: AES Tech (CEO Jaehong Jeffrey Chun) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held on July 30. Organizers arranged this meetup to inform overseas media about participating companies’ products and technologies in advance for global markets while expanding business opportunities. AES Tech joined this meetup as a company submitting its modular hydrogen supply system ‘ammoNOVA Ultra’—which extracts hydrogen on-site from liquid ammonia—for the CES 2027 Innovation Awards, with CEO Jaehong Jeffrey Chun delivering the presentation on this day.

A surge in power demand triggered by AI lies in the background. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects global data center electricity consumption to more than double from approximately 415 TWh in 2024 to around 945 TWh by 2030. The core challenge is that power grid connections and new power generation facilities struggle to keep pace with the construction speed of data centers. Consequently, a trend to place dedicated power generation sources near data centers emerged, and gas turbines capable of fast startup, output adjustment, and short installation periods surfaced as a realistic alternative. However, because burning natural gas leaves carbon emissions, gradually increasing hydrogen co-firing ratios requires hydrogen supply systems as well as generators to move in sync with gas turbine operational changes.

blocks.cap: Illustration depicting a 4-unit parallel configuration of AES Tech’s ammonia-based on-site hydrogen production module ‘ammoNOVA Ultra’ | Image provided by AES Tech

blocks.x: Conventional hydrogen supply methods face clear limits here. Transporting central-produced hydrogen via tube trailers continuously incurs compression, storage, transportation, and safety management costs, making it difficult to supply large-volume flow rates consistently. Thermal crackers using ammonia as a raw material must maintain high temperatures continuously, creating thermal inertia in responding to startups and load fluctuations. The exact point AES Tech targets is “producing hydrogen on-site immediately as much as needed.”

ammoNOVA Ultra is a 20-foot standard module that electrochemically extracts hydrogen from anhydrous liquid ammonia. Because it controls reactions by supplying electric current to electrochemical stacks instead of decomposing ammonia with heat, hydrogen production volume connects directly with stack current, allowing it to follow second- and minute-by-minute gas turbine load fluctuations. Design goals presented by the company include daily hydrogen production of approximately 240 pounds, operation at 10 to 100 percent output, load fluctuation tracking of 40 percentage points within 1 minute, 99.999 percent hydrogen purity, and ammonia slip below 50 ppmv. Company officials explain that these represent design targets for commercial modules, distinguished from current achieved values.

blocks.cap: AES Tech CEO Jaehong Jeffrey Chun (left) during an interview with Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Core differentiators reside in stack structure and emission characteristics. AES Tech’s ‘SCC’ structure aims to integrate serration-based sealing, rear-side cooling channels on separator plates, uniform clamping via bending and leaf springs, and shunt current suppression channels into a single stack, eliminating separate cooling cells and reducing stack length by over 30 percent. Furthermore, because oxygen does not participate in the electrolysis process, it avoids the nitrogen oxide (NOx) emission issues that thermochemical methods face when decomposing ammonia at high temperatures. Unhydrogenated ammonia remaining after reactions is recirculated in a closed loop rather than discarded, through which the company targets an energy efficiency of over 90 percent.

The system also took scalability into account. Because large gas turbines require more hydrogen than a single module provides, instead of indefinitely scaling up equipment, standard 20-foot modules connect in parallel via a common header to expand incrementally from 1 to 4 units, operating remaining modules even during maintenance of specific units. Combined with this is the control platform ‘ACE-UP’, which collects sensor data in real time to compare against normal operation models and detect abnormal signs early. The company explains this not as complete autonomous operation, but as a control platform stage assisting anomaly detection and operational judgment.

blocks.cap: Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen (left) and AES Tech CEO Jaehong Jeffrey Chun take a commemorative photo after concluding the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: In the US, cases of large AI and cloud corporations alongside power generation companies introducing gas turbines directly at data center sites rather than waiting for grid connections are increasing, and AES Tech targets fuel supply for hydrogen co-firing in this trend. Domestically, the company executes empirical projects with government support. Currently commercializing a compact product half the size of a 20-foot unit to supply development-demand companies, the company will unveil its full commercial model, ammoNOVA Ultra, for the first time at CES 2027.

Jaehong Jeffrey Chun, CEO of AES Tech, explained, “Even if gas turbines offer power flexibility for AI, burning natural gas leaves carbon emissions at the combustion stage.” He added, “The goal is to produce hydrogen on-site from ammonia as much as needed, gradually raising the co-firing ratio.” He continued, saying, “However, clean characteristics are not guaranteed automatically, and environmental benefits materialize when electricity used and ammonia production pathways are low-carbon.”

Meanwhile, AVING News has promoted South Korean companies worldwide through media partnerships with over 800 outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building upon its global media network, AVING News newly launched the ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ last August. Global US IT and tech media outlet Ubergizmo participated in this ‘Global Media Meetup’.

t: [CES Innovation Awards 2027 Special] Pinos Korea Challenges CES 2027 Innovation Awards with Constraint-Aware AI ‘PINOS-X’ Supporting Multi-Country Wellness Launch Decisions

blocks.cap: Howard Han Do Kim, CEO of Pinos Korea, delivers a presentation. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Pinos Korea (CEO Howard Han Do Kim) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held on July 30. Organizers arranged this meetup to inform overseas media about participating companies’ products and technologies in advance for global markets while expanding business opportunities. Pinos Korea joined this meetup as a company challenging the CES 2027 Innovation Awards with its constraint-aware B2B AI platform ‘PINOS-X’, which assists decision-making for developing and launching global wellness products in complex regulatory environments. CEO Howard Han Do Kim delivered the presentation on this day.

PINOS-X targets high-cost decision-making problems arising before actual capital deployment. When wellness companies prepare for multi-country launches, scientific evidence, ingredient dosages, safety, labeling and advertising claims, formulations, manufacturing readiness, pricing, distribution margin structures, and country-specific regulations are usually reviewed separately. While a change in a single condition can invalidate multiple subsequent decisions, such conflicts often surface only after costs for formulation development, manufacturing preparation, or market entry have already been incurred.

blocks.cap: Application example of Pinos Korea’s AI decision platform ‘PINOS-X’ depicted via AI-generated image | Image provided by Pinos Korea

blocks.x: PINOS-X converts these scattered inputs into interconnected, version-controlled constraints. Orchestrating eight analytical modules—including regulatory intelligence, scientific evidence, formulation design, market analysis, and business feasibility—it links and propagates a single controlled constraint across five key decision-making domains: formulation, labeling/advertising, manufacturing readiness, business feasibility, and launch prioritization. If specific ingredient dosages or claims conflict with a country’s requirements, the system identifies the conflict, reviews suitable alternatives, and recalculates impacted assumptions, deriving assumptions by simulating each scenario at least 10,000 times. Results are presented as country-specific directions to proceed (GO), modify (ADAPT), or hold (HOLD). Even for the same product, different conclusions emerge by country—such as HOLD for the US, ADAPT for South Korea, and GO for the UAE—and PINOS-X guides markets receiving a GO rating as launch priorities.

To ensure reliability, each analytical result receives a unique ‘Run ID’ containing evidence sources, version information, assumptions, risk factors, reviewed alternatives, unresolved exceptions, expert review points, and next actions. Users can manage AI outputs not as one-off answers, but as traceable decision-making records. The company emphasizes that PINOS-X is not a system for diagnosis or medical practice, but a human-in-the-loop decision-support software that enhances rather than replaces expert judgment. Regarding this core structure, Pinos Korea filed a domestic patent titled ‘Integrated System for Nutraceutical Formulation Design, Regulatory Analysis, and Business Feasibility Evaluation Based on Multi-Module GPT Orchestration’, preparing with a target first market launch date of January 7, 2027.

blocks.cap: Pinos Korea CEO Howard Han Do Kim (right) during an interview with Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Since its establishment in 2024, Pinos Korea has accumulated field experience by executing healthcare and biotech commercialization services—including global market entry strategies, regulatory/feasibility reviews, R&D-linked business development, and international partnership building—reflecting this expertise into PINOS-X’s constraint models and decision workflows. Current revenues stem from these professional services, while product revenues such as subscriptions or licenses for PINOS-X do not yet exist. In 2026, the company formed an official partnership with Canada’s Mila (Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute) to jointly advance knowledge retrieval, constraint-aware verification, guardrails, and evaluation methodologies, while establishing ‘PINOS AURÉON Intelligence Artificielle Inc.’ in Quebec as a long-term hub for North American AI and healthcare collaboration.

For market entry, the company prioritizes reviewing the US and Canada, followed by step-by-step expansion into Australia, Germany, and key ASEAN countries like Malaysia and Vietnam. In Australia and Germany in particular, the company discusses formulation suitability, production feasibility, quality requirements, and supply terms with local manufacturing partners regarding digital wellness products analyzed via PINOS-X. However, these remain at early commercialization and manufacturing readiness verification stages rather than finalized production or export contracts. Targeting small-to-medium enterprises preparing multi-country launches, product development/regulatory/quality leads, CDMOs, ingredient suppliers, distributors, and brand enterprises rather than general consumers, the company primarily pursues a model combining B2B subscriptions, guided pilots, and professional services.

t: [CES Innovation Awards 2027 Special] A.I.MATICS Submits AI Vision Inspection Platform ‘AIM-T1’ for CES 2027 Innovation Awards… Automating Inspection with Just 5 Good Samples

blocks.cap: Jaewon Lee, AI LAB Specialist at A.I.MATICS, delivers a presentation. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: A.I.MATICS (CEO Victor Hoon Lee) participated in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ held on July 30. Organizers arranged this meetup to inform overseas media about participating companies’ products and technologies in advance for global markets while expanding business opportunities. A.I.MATICS joined this meetup as a company submitting its AI vision inspection platform ‘AIM-T1’ for the CES 2027 Innovation Awards, with Jaewon Lee, AI LAB Specialist at A.I.MATICS, delivering the presentation on this day.

A.I.MATICS launched in 2003 as an in-house venture of Hyundai Motor Group before growing into an independent entity. Researching on-device vision AI for autonomous driving that requires immediate judgments in high-speed driving environments for over 10 years, the company secured patent-based ‘World Model AI’ and its proprietary engine ‘aimNet’. Running directly on devices without cloud dependencies, aimNet serves as a real-time AI engine that the company applied to over 520,000 vehicles, accumulating driving data equivalent to approximately 3,500 years (11 million video clips, 34 TB) alongside over 104 domestic and international patents. A.I.MATICS expands its recognition intelligence—verified in mobility—into high-volume electronics manufacturing environments where precision holds paramount importance.

blocks.cap: AI vision inspection platform ‘AIM-T1’ by A.I.MATICS | Image provided by A.I.MATICS

blocks.x: Structural challenges such as ‘reshoring’ and ‘skilled labor shortages’ lie in the background. According to the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA), private investments exceeding 770 billion USD across more than 160 semiconductor projects were announced in 30 US states since 2020, while Deloitte and others project 1.9 million US manufacturing jobs to remain unfilled by 2033. While factories expand rapidly, skilled inspection personnel who guarantee quality cannot keep pace. In particular, inspection sites require over 72 hours to gather new defect datasets, manually adjust thresholds, and retrain AI models whenever products change, relying on the experience of a few skilled inspectors for micron-level pass/fail decisions. This expertise does not transfer easily to other factories.

AIM-T1 directly targets this problem. Its core patent-based ‘World Model AI’ learns object structures and surface textures in advance through self-supervised learning before seeing products, thereby generating new product inspection criteria using only 3 to 5 good reference samples without defect images. Combined with In-Context Learning and the AIM Automatic Training System (AATS), this shortened AI model transition time during New Product Introduction (NPI) from approximately 72 hours to about 4 hours. Because inspection criteria reside in software rather than hardware, even when products change, teams avoid rebuilding inspection equipment, reusing a single platform across multiple products and lines.

blocks.cap: A.I.MATICS AI LAB Specialist Jaewon Lee during an interview with Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: The difference from conventional methods lies in ‘what the system learns’. Rule-based systems (AOI) require humans to set thresholds, while supervised learning AI learns thousands of defect images per product, necessitating model rebuilds when products change. Conversely, AIM-T1 understands the object itself rather than a list of defects, determining flaws based on deviation from normal states to catch undefined defects. Designed for field quality engineers rather than AI experts, usage follows three simple steps: selecting good samples on-screen (Drag), confirming normal criteria formed by the system (Teach), and starting inspection (Inspect). This allows in-house quality teams—rather than external AI vendors or system integrators (SI)—to execute product switchovers directly. Hardware adopts a modular structure, adjusting camera resolution, quantity, direction, lens magnification, and lighting to fit products, applying liquid lens electronic focus stacking. Hence, it mounts directly onto existing production lines without separate inspection rooms or line redesigns.

Results emerged from real production sites. An initial version (1.0) of AIM-T1 operates on connector assembly lines at a major Korean conglomerate’s electronics production base in Vietnam, verifying up to 75,000 daily inspections, 100% detection of irregular defects, a 0.01% escape rate, and a 26% productivity boost. Catching defects as small as 10 μm, its 700 mm integrated housing operates in sync with existing line tact times. Reflecting field experiences, the company recently released its next-generation version, ‘AIM-T1 2.0’.

blocks.cap: Ubergizmo Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen, A.I.MATICS AI LAB Specialist Jaewon Lee, and officials take a commemorative photo after concluding the Global Media Meetup. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: Market expansion accelerates in earnest as well. Currently applied to camera modules, semiconductor packages, and PCB/FPCB assembly inspections, AIM-T1 plans to expand into automotive electronic components, displays, and batteries. Using its Vietnam entity as a hub to solidify its position in Southeast Asian markets, A.I.MATICS plans step-by-step entry into North America—where semiconductor, battery, and electronics reshoring expands—and South America, centered on automotive and electronic components. To this end, the company expands collaborations with global manufacturing enterprises, automation equipment partners, and system integration firms.

Jaewon Lee, AI LAB Specialist at A.I.MATICS who delivered the presentation, stated, “Because problems differ across industries, we need industry-specialized AI rather than a single general-purpose AI.” He added, “Converting inspection expertise into software-based scalable manufacturing capabilities, we will target the global manufacturing market with an AI inspection platform that responds without retraining even when products change.”

t: [CES Innovation Awards 2027 Special] BizCrush Targets CES 2027 with Real-Time Multilingual Meeting AI Operating Amid Background Noise… “Proving Performance Through Open Benchmarks”

blocks.cap: BizCrush CEO Taemin Kwak presents at the Global Media Meetup event. | Photo by AVING News

blocks.x: BizCrush, Inc. (CEO Taemin Kwak) participated on Monday, the 27th, in the ‘Global Media Meetup’ hosted for domestic companies and startups by AVING News’ ‘International Press Club (IPC)’ at the MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

Running for four days from July 27 to 30, this ‘Global Media Meetup’ focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to report to global media in advance on the products and technologies of companies participating in global exhibitions, including CES 2027, and to expand business opportunities. BizCrush CEO Taemin Kwak delivered the presentation on this day.

Backed by Google for Startups and operating as a US Delaware C-Corp with a Korean entity, BizCrush is an AI technology pioneer specializing in real-time, multilingual speech recognition, translation, and automated meeting record generation. Founded by CEO Taemin Kwak (holding more than 9 registered patents), who developed production systems in STT (speech-to-text) and natural language processing fields for over 8 years, and CTO Ethan Kim (Jaeyeop Kim), a Google open-source contributor, the company was established in 2025 on a global-market premise from the outset. Ahead of its official commercial Enterprise release, BizCrush is actively building its global presence by exhibiting at CES 2027 in Las Vegas and entering its proprietary technology into the CES 2027 Innovation Awards in AI Software & Mobile Apps and Accessibility.

BizCrush assists communication with real-time subtitles and translation while meetings progress, connecting conversations to summaries, follow-up tasks, and meeting minutes after meetings end. Its voice pipeline automatically recognizes 60 languages without separate configurations and processes conversations where languages switch within a single sentence. It delivers real-time performance across iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows, serving subtitles within 0.4 to 0.5 seconds of the utterance, translations in about 2.5 seconds, and listener-specific AI voice dubbing within 5 seconds.

Its core competitiveness lies in ‘accuracy in actual operating environments.’ In quiet lab environments, recognition error rates for major services appear to be similar, at around 4–6 percent. Still, in real environments with background noise, such as cafes or event venues, error rates soar. BizCrush approaches this issue with a patent-pending on-device speech enhancement engine that filters out ambient noise and refines speech inside user devices before audio reaches recognition engines. Furthermore, it operates a public benchmark platform that publishes measurement methodologies, raw audio data, and competitors’ outputs. As of July 2026, its Character Error Rate (CER) in high-noise environments with loud background sounds reached the 41 percent range—lower than competing services at 46 to 60 percent—and its overall average error rate was 22.8 percent, the lowest among services listed on the benchmark.

blocks.cap: ‘BizCrush’ mobile and web screens | Image provided by BizCrush

blocks.x: Products include subscription apps for individuals and teams ($7.99 to $29.99/month) and on-site solutions for conferences and exhibitions. The on-site solution broadcasts stage utterances as real-time translated subtitles on large screens, allowing attendees to receive subtitles in their own languages on their mobile devices by simply scanning a QR code without installing an app or signing up. It also supports interpretation and recording in 1-on-1 consultation booths. Adding an ‘adaptive glossary’ to this, users register terminology in advance or upload PDFs to configure initial dictionaries, and recognition accuracy steadily rises as the system learns user names, technical terminology, and abbreviations over repeated meetings. Built with privacy in mind by the architecture, it also offers a “Privacy Mode” where live scripts stream without saving audio recordings, while allowing secure export directly to a client’s private storage or Notion.

Track records accumulate as well. BizCrush operated real-time transcription and translation solutions across 12 events and sites in Korea and the US in 2026 alone. In the US, it signed an MOU with the Korean Education Center in Seattle to support the 2026 PNW Korean Speaking Contest and conducted a pilot with Lynnwood, Washington. Participating as an official technology partner in ‘Korean Night with Carmen’ co-hosted by the Consulate General of the Republic of Korea in Seattle and Seattle Opera, it operated American events such as Georgia KAGC 2026 and Auburn University’s AUAI AI Summit in Alabama. In Korea, it handled real-time subtitles and translations for major conferences including Skill-Up Festa 2026, WIS 2026, and Changbal Dev Conference. In the corporate sector, domestic call centers adopted it as an AI Contact Center (AICC) case, leading to additional contracts and discussions on on-premise expansion. According to BizCrush, paid customers have increased each month since the initial paid payments were introduced in January 2026, and monthly revenue has grown more than threefold since full-scale billing started in March.

BizCrush launches its official commercial version ‘BizCrush Enterprise’ on August 31. The company submitted this product to the CES 2027 Innovation Awards in three categories: Artificial Intelligence, Software & Mobile Apps, and Accessibility, and plans to showcase it as a live working demo at the CES 2027 Eureka Park booth. Officials selected BizCrush for the Ministry of Science and ICT’s K-Tech Pioneers and Google’s Chang-Goo Program, and the company participated in San Francisco’s MARU Accelerator Program.

BizCrush CEO Taemin Kwak stated, “In quiet demonstration environments, performance differences between speech recognition services do not show clearly, but exhibition halls with constant background noise and dozens of languages passing through represent the actual usage environment itself.” He added, “With a structure where conversations at the booth become product demonstrations, showing actual environment performance as it is on the global stage of CES serves as the primary purpose of participation.” He continued, “Allowing anyone to verify performance claims directly on the open benchmark and presenting execution plans through concrete milestones with dates, we will build trust in global markets step by step.”
